note: All rev-3 findings (0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 3 NIT) were applied to design.md in revision 4: category OG-route slug regex unified to ^[a-z0-9-]{1,120}$ in both routes and the §10 validator (matching categorySchema max(120)); the seoAuto master kill-switch is now wired via a single mergeFeatures(config.features) gate at the top of runProductSeo/runCategorySeo/runAuditSweep, referenced in §6.1/§6.9/§11; invalidateSeoCaches() now clears both the 'sitemap' and 'robots' cache keys (§6.9/§13/§15); the JSON-LD image argument is documented as left unchanged (§5.1/§6.8); and the §6.2 queue skip uses the same ATTENTION_THRESHOLD as the needs-attention predicate. See 'Responses to design review (revision 4)' in design.md.

findings.title: Category OG-route slug regex conflicts with real category slug length and with §10
findings.problem: categorySchema.slug is max(120) in routes/admin.ts, so stored category slugs can be 81-120 chars. The {1,80} regex copied from the page route would 404 the new GET /api/og/category/:slug and /api/og/image/category/:slug for valid long slugs, silently breaking the category share HTML and share image. §6.6 and §10 also disagree (80 vs 120).
findings.fix: Use ^[a-z0-9-]{1,120}$ in both new category OG routes and in the §10 optimize.category validator, matching categorySchema max(120); state in §6.6 that the category bound is 120 (not the page route's 80) and why.
findings.resolution: §6.6 now uses ^[a-z0-9-]{1,120}$ for both GET /api/og/category/:slug and GET /api/og/image/category/:slug and adds a sentence explaining the 120 bound (vs the page route's 80) because category slugs can be 81-120 chars. §10 optimize.category already used {1,120}; the two now agree.

findings.title: seoAuto master feature flag declared but never wired to the auto-generation hooks
findings.where: §3/§7/§14 declare seoAuto; §6.1, §5.3, §6.9 describe hooks/cron as unconditional
findings.problem: The brief requires high-impact automation to be feature-flagged. The flag is added and merge logic verified (utils/features.ts), but no write path (POST /products hook, import audit enqueue, 15-min cron) is said to read seoAuto. As written seoAuto=false would not disable automation — the kill-switch is cosmetic. The design also never names where server-side features are loaded for the gate.
findings.fix: Specify a single gate point in runProductSeo/runCategorySeo/runAuditSweep that reads mergeFeatures(...) and early-returns when seoAuto is off; name the server-side features source (e.g. config.features, same blob POST /api/admin/features writes); add the gate to §6.1, §6.9 and the §11 invariant table.
findings.resolution: §6.1 now specifies a single gate at the top of runProductSeo/runCategorySeo/runAuditSweep that reads mergeFeatures(loadStoredFeatures()) over the config.features blob (the same source POST /api/admin/features writes) and early-returns when seoAuto is off. §6.1.2 (import audit enqueue) and §6.9 (15-min cron) reference the gate, and §11 adds an invariant row. The kill-switch now disables the create/update hook, import audit enqueue, and cron while leaving commerce untouched.

findings.title: invalidateSitemapCache() must also bust the robots cache entry
findings.problem: routes/seo.ts caches two keys ('sitemap' and 'robots') in one Map; clearing only 'sitemap' leaves a stale robots.txt for up to 5 min after a policy change. The function name implies sitemap-only.
findings.fix: Export a function that clears both keys (or cache.clear()), e.g. invalidateSeoCaches(); reference it in §6.9/§13/§15.
findings.resolution: §6.9 step 2 now defines invalidateSeoCaches() clearing both 'sitemap' and 'robots'; §13 and §15 reference the renamed function.

findings.title: JSON-LD image argument semantics under-specified vs the real call site
findings.problem: routes/og.ts passes JSON-LD image as absoluteImageUrl(product.og_image || product.image) || renderedCard. The design does not state whether generateProductSeo should touch this call site; silence invites an implementer to change crawler output.
findings.fix: Add a sentence to §5.1/§6.8: the existing JSON-LD image resolution is left unchanged; the engine only adds imageAlt and never rewrites the builder's image argument.
findings.resolution: §5.1 and §6.8 now state the existing JSON-LD image resolution (og_image || product.image || rendered card) is left unchanged; the engine only adds imageAlt and never rewrites the builder's image argument.

findings.title: needs-attention predicate and idempotent-skip predicate use an unreconciled threshold
findings.problem: Only ATTENTION_THRESHOLD is pinned. If the queue skip threshold differs, an entity could be skipped by the optimizer yet flagged 'needs attention' on the dashboard (or vice-versa).
findings.fix: State that the queue skip uses the same ATTENTION_THRESHOLD (score >= ATTENTION_THRESHOLD AND no problems AND unchanged hash => skip).
findings.resolution: §6.2 now states the queue idempotent-skip uses the same ATTENTION_THRESHOLD constant (§5.4): skip when seo_score >= ATTENTION_THRESHOLD AND no seo_problems AND unchanged seo_source_hash, so the two surfaces can never disagree.
